- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). 576	// foldedLike renders a case-insensitive LIKE comparison of colExpr against a
577	// (already metacharacter-escaped) pattern, using each dialect's case-folding.
578	func (r *renderer) foldedLike(colExpr, pattern string) string {
579		switch r.dialect {
580		case DialectSQLite:
581			// memos_unicode_lower gives Unicode-aware folding; ESCAPE '\' is required
582			// because SQLite has no default LIKE escape character.

585			// ILIKE is case-insensitive; backslash is the default escape character.
586			return fmt.Sprintf("%s ILIKE %s", colExpr, r.addArg(pattern))
587		default: // MySQL: default collation is case-insensitive; backslash is the default escape.
588			return fmt.Sprintf("%s LIKE %s", colExpr, r.addArg(pattern))
589		}

593	func likePattern(mode TextMatchMode, value string) string {
594		escaped := escapeLikeLiteral(value)
595		switch mode {

598		case TextMatchSuffix:
599			return "%" + escaped

607	func escapeLikeLiteral(s string) string {

623		}
624	
625		if cond.Kind == ComprehensionExistsOne {

627		}

632			return r.renderTagEquals(field, pred.Value, cond.Kind)
633		case *StartsWithPredicate:

644	// renderTagAll renders tags.all(t, <pred>): the array is non-empty AND no element
645	// fails the predicate. Element predicates use plain CEL semantics (case-insensitive

647	func (r *renderer) renderTagAll(field Field, pred PredicateExpr) (renderResult, error) {
648		arrayExpr := jsonArrayExpr(r.dialect, field)
649		elemCond, err := r.elementPredicateSQL(pred)

652		}
653		switch r.dialect {
654		case DialectSQLite:
655			nonEmpty := fmt.Sprintf("%s IS NOT NULL AND %s != '[]'", arrayExpr, arrayExpr)
656			sub := fmt.Sprintf("NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(%s) WHERE NOT (%s))", arrayExpr, elemCond)
657			return renderResult{sql: fmt.Sprintf("(%s AND %s)", nonEmpty, sub)}, nil
658		case DialectMySQL:
659			nonEmpty := fmt.Sprintf("%s IS NOT NULL AND JSON_LENGTH(%s) > 0", arrayExpr, arrayExpr)

662		case DialectPostgres:

668		}

671	// renderTagExistsOne renders tags.exists_one(t, <pred>): exactly one element
672	// satisfies the predicate, via a COUNT(...) = 1 subquery. A null or empty array
673	// yields COUNT 0, which is correctly not equal to 1.
674	func (r *renderer) renderTagExistsOne(field Field, pred PredicateExpr) (renderResult, error) {
675		arrayExpr := jsonArrayExpr(r.dialect, field)
676		elemCond, err := r.elementPredicateSQL(pred)
677		if err != nil {
678			return renderResult{}, err
679		}
680		switch r.dialect {
681		case DialectSQLite:
682			return renderResult{sql: fmt.Sprintf("(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM json_each(%s) WHERE %s) = 1", arrayExpr, elemCond)}, nil
683		case DialectMySQL:
684			return renderResult{sql: fmt.Sprintf("(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM JSON_TABLE(%s, '$[*]' COLUMNS (value VARCHAR(512) PATH '$')) AS elem WHERE %s) = 1", arrayExpr, elemCond)}, nil
685		case DialectPostgres:
686			return renderResult{sql: fmt.Sprintf("(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text(%s) AS elem(value) WHERE %s) = 1", arrayExpr, elemCond)}, nil
687		default:
688			return renderResult{}, errors.Errorf("unsupported dialect %s", r.dialect)
689		}
690	}

692	// elementPredicateSQL builds the per-element SQL condition for an all() predicate.
693	// The iterated element is exposed as the unqualified column `value` on all dialects
694	// (json_each.value / JSON_TABLE column / elem(value)).
695	func (r *renderer) elementPredicateSQL(pred PredicateExpr) (string, error) {
696		switch p := pred.(type) {
697		case *EqualsPredicate:
698			return fmt.Sprintf("value = %s", r.addArg(p.Value)), nil
699		case *StartsWithPredicate:
700			return r.foldedLike("value", likePattern(TextMatchPrefix, p.Prefix)), nil
701		case *EndsWithPredicate:
702			return r.foldedLike("value", likePattern(TextMatchSuffix, p.Suffix)), nil
703		case *ContainsPredicate:
704			return r.foldedLike("value", likePattern(TextMatchContains, p.Substring)), nil
705		default:
706			return "", errors.Errorf("unsupported predicate %T in all()", pred)
707		}
708	}
